newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latin American stocks seen quiet in Christmas week.
newsitem.headline: Latin American stocks seen quiet in Christmas week.

text.p: Latin American stock markets are expected to remain quiet this week as investors and traders look more toward a big Christmas dinner than a big stocks rally, analysts said.
Investors are looking at shortened trading sessions in what is expected to be slow trade this week.
Brazil shares are seen set for a short and sluggish week as the bourses close Tuesday and Wednesday for Christmas holidays, brokers and analysts said.
"Activity is likely to be very weak because of the holidays," a trader said.
Analysts said worries over the re-election debate in Congress, after scheduled votes on the issue were delayed, could also help slowing trading.

Last week, Brazilian shares rose 3.9 percent to 69,422 points amid heavy buying of telecommunications stocks. On Friday, trading volume fell to 356.8 million reais ($343 million) from the recent daily average of 600-700 million reais.
After rising 3.31 percent last week, the Mexican stock market is expected to post an apathetic performance this holiday week.
Analysts expect the market to trade in a narrow band between 3,120 and 3,320 points, before making a modest year-end rally.
But the conflict in Peru and what is considered to be an undervalued Mexican market could help make Mexico more of a favorite among emerging markets, analysts said.
Moderate declines in interest rates and better returns in the construction, steel and consumer goods sectors are also seen helping the country's market.
Argentine stocks were expected to ease gently in slack volume as cash flows ebb in the last full week of 1997, dealers said.
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index rallied 4.6 percent last week to close at 628, erasing the previous week's heavy losses.

"The market may be heading for a logical correction," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "It weathered last Friday's options expirations but could now slip to around 613 as liquidity becomes tighter around the Christmas and New Year breaks."

Traders predicted any new estimates of domestic tax revenue and industrial production were likely to be favorable, and said investors would keep tabs on Wall Street and the movement of the U.S. long bond yields.
"Our market remains very conditioned by what happens in New York," said Bonanno.
Chilean stocks are seen steady but with a slightly negative tilt this week in thin Christmas trade, said dealers.
"It looks like a pretty regular week. The light volume means we won't be able to see any firm trend," said one dealer.

Electricity shares, which account for a 40-percent weighting in the IPSA index are expected to remain wobbly on fears over the impact of this year's drought on hydro-electric generators' profits, said brokers.
The 40-share index ended last week off 0.54 percent at 88.66 points. The general index shed 0.34 percent to 4,893 points.
With trade winding down and most Caracas businesses already shut for the Christmas break, brokers see only quiet trade for Venezuela for the coming week.
Nevertheless, "despite the holidays and a seasonally quiet market, we continue to recommend Venezuelan equities over the long term," said local brokers Merinvest in a research note.

Last week, the Caracas bolsa spurted ahead on the successful auctions of state-owned Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado, with the leading 19-share index rising 2.2 percent to close Friday at 6,349.47 points.
((-- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559))
